claim: For the modified Nosé–Hoover system \(\dot x=y\), \(\dot y=-x-yz\), and \(\dot z=\alpha(y^2-1-\varepsilon z)\), with fixed \(\alpha>0\), the surface \(M_{1/\varepsilon}=\{z=(y^2-1)/\varepsilon\}\) used in the published large-\(\varepsilon\) argument is not invariant: for \(Q=z-(y^2-1)/\varepsilon\), \(\dot Q=-\alpha\varepsilon Q+(2/\varepsilon)y(x+yz)\), so on \(M_{1/\varepsilon}\) the normal defect is generically nonzero, and the only complete trajectory contained in that surface is the equilibrium \( (0,0,-1/\varepsilon)\). Nevertheless, the large-dissipation conclusion can be repaired and strengthened. There exists \(\varepsilon_0(\alpha)\) such that for every \(\varepsilon>\varepsilon_0(\alpha)\) the full three-dimensional system has an asymptotically stable nonconstant periodic orbit. Its \((x,y)\)-projection converges to the circle \(x^2+y^2=4/3\) as \(\varepsilon\to\infty\), and on the attracting slow manifold \(z=\varepsilon^{-1}(y^2-1)+(2/(\alpha\varepsilon^2))xy+O(\varepsilon^{-3})\) on a compact annulus containing that cycle.
limitations: The theorem is asymptotic for fixed \(\alpha>0\) and does not provide an explicit \(\varepsilon\) threshold, global basin, or classification of other recurrent sets. The slow-manifold expansion is local to a fixed compact annulus around the selected cycle.
scientific_integrity: The nullcline defect and asymptotic coefficients are reconstructed from the printed differential equations. No numerical trajectory is used as proof. Existence and stability invoke standard Fenichel persistence and first-order averaging on a compact annulus; independent audit has not been performed.
title: Corrected large-dissipation periodic-orbit theorem for the modified Nosé–Hoover oscillator
